comments.author: @HiddenCanada
comments.text:
In 1996, a small hole on top of Bennett Dam revealed damage deep inside the structure. The dam was repaired, but imagine living downstream and hearing about that discovery.

If you lived in Hudson's Hope, Peace River, or anywhere along the Peace River, would you feel safe knowing such a massive reservoir was upstream?

I'd especially love to hear from anyone who remembers the 1996 incident or has worked at the dam.

And just to be clear, the failure shown in this video is hypothetical. There is no indication from the safety reports reviewed that the dam is facing imminent failure.

comments.author: @dralexmclean
comments.text: I was an engineer working in BCFP's Mackenzie pulp mill when the lake finally came up to full flood in the spring of 72.  We had built the mills fresh water intake pumps on the flat land beside the (before the lake filled) Parsnip river.  It was very cool to watch the lake flood and cover the Pump house that we had built.  As you indicated large parts of the forest were left unlogged as the lake rose.  Parked at the entrance into Mackenzie is a Huge Tree Crusher built by the LeTourneau corporation which it had been hoped would be able to walk thru the forest knocking down trees so they would float up and be recovered when flooded.  Reality was the Crusher got VERY stuck in the bush just north of Mackenzie.  We would sometimes walk by it (embedded in the bush) when fishing the creeks feeding into Williston.  Lets hope the Damn holds!!

comments.author: @winstonsmith935
comments.text: All dams in the world are subject to increased Hydrology Changes around the world. The term the media uses is Rivers of Rain, aka the PINE Apple Express

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: You’re referring to atmospheric rivers, the Pineapple Express is a particular pattern carrying moisture from near Hawaii toward the West Coast. The key question for Bennett is how much water reaches its watershed and how the reservoir and spillway handle it.

comments.author: @alancadieux2984
comments.text: Drove along hwy 29 from fsj to a few km from Hudson's hope, several times in the last year, in places the hwy is very low to near the water level. In a dam failure, only with advance warning ⚠️ would this route work, since you aren't clear of the flood problem until you are close to fsj. The only end result is completely catastrophic along the entire river valley. Every reservoir in the world 🌎 has the sediment problem, when the flood picks it up and moves it, and it will, everywhere the flood spreads out will change alot in it's future. No boats are allowed in or on the site C dam reservoir due to the hillsides softening and collapsing into the water, trees are floating everywhere, and the tsunami waves are considered to be an unpredictable hazard. Lots of risk for the "benefits" considered to be "gained."

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Thanks for sharing that, Alan. That’s the concern I raised about Highway 29: a route used for a wildfire evacuation can’t automatically be treated as a safe way out during a dam breach. Hearing from someone who’s driven those stretches adds useful context.
